reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general high-temperature tribo-oxidation and glaze-layer formation in CCAs but provides no specific data on boron doping, B2O3 formation, or its lubricating effect in CoCrFeNi. The key premises about boron gradient, B2O3 lubrication, and quantitative friction reduction are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Boron doping of CoCrFeNi surface creates a boron-enriched gradient
Above ~600 °C in oxidizing atmosphere, surface boron oxidizes to form lubricious B2O3 film
B2O3 film provides self-healing solid lubrication, reducing friction and wear by 25–35%
Below ~600 °C, boron-doped layer does not significantly affect friction
Tribo-oxidation at high temperatures can form protective glaze layers that reduce wear
